title: Tabular Foundation Models for Credit Risk Prediction: A Dedicated Review and Empirical Comparison
abstract: arXiv:2605.18147v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Predictive models are central to credit risk management, where the accuracy of default-probability and loss estimates affects the profitability of lending and the stability of the financial system. Decades of benchmarking research have consolidated the state of the art, with gradient-boosting models often representing the strongest machine-learning benchmark, while linear and logistic models remain important regulatory and industry reference models. The recent advent of tabular data foundation models introduces a new paradigm for predictive modeling. Rather than fitting a model to a target dataset, they use in-context learning to integrate information from the target dataset with prior knowledge acquired through large-scale pretraining on diverse collections of (synthetic) tabular data. translated_title: 用于信用风险预测的表格基础模型：专门综述与实证比较
translated_abstract: 预测模型是信用风险管理的核心，违约概率和损失估计的准确性直接影响贷款业务的盈利能力和金融系统的稳定性。数十年的基准测试研究已经巩固了现有技术水平：梯度提升模型通常代表最强的机器学习基准，而线性模型和逻辑回归模型仍然是重要的监管与行业参考模型。近期出现的表格数据基础模型为预测建模引入了一种新范式——它们不再将模型拟合到目标数据集上，而是通过上下文学习，将来自目标数据集的信息与通过在多样化（合成）表格数据集合上进行大规模预训练所获得的先验知识相结合。我们推测，获取目标数据之外的信息在小数据场景中是有益的，并且可能有助于解决长期存在的挑战……
tldr: 本文系统综述并实证比较了表格基础模型在信用风险预测中的应用，指出其借助上下文学习利用大规模预训练先验知识，有望在小数据场景下超越梯度提升等传统模型并解决长期存在的挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a dedicated review and empirical comparison of tabular foundation models for credit risk prediction, showing that their in-context learning leverages large-scale pretraining priors and may outperform gradient-boosting benchmarks, especially in small-data settings.
